name: Awbono
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Awbono known essentially from survey wordlists; no grammar or phonology located

sources.citation: Mukhamdanah & Inayatusshalihah. 2021. Bahasa Awban di Yahukimo, Papua: kajian awal terhadap bahasa minoritas pada tataran fonologi dan leksikonnya (Awban Language in Yahukimo, Papua: A Preliminary Study on Phonology and Lexicon Aspect toward a Minority Language). Sawerigading 27(2): 219-229. doi:10.26499/sawer.v27i2.931 (Indonesian).
sources.note: Nothing. The phonology section (pp. 223-226) gives only a vowel inventory (8 vowels) and consonant inventory (18 consonants) with positional distribution from a 400-item survey list; phonemic status left undecided. The word 'tekanan' (stress) appears once, p. 222, in a general theory paragraph quoting Hafsah et al. 2018 ('bunyi suprasegmental: tekanan, nada, panjang, dan intonasi'), not as a statement about Awban. Transcriptions show vowel length ([ti:] 'dog', [nE:h] 'bird') but no stress marks.

sources.citation: Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa. 2019. Bahasa dan Peta Bahasa di Indonesia, p. 219 (entry 'Awban', also called 'Bese').
sources.note: Official Indonesian language-map entry; may carry a short phonological note; at least fixes the identity Awban = Awbono and the village location.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. 2018 (text version 2019-11-11). Annotated Swadesh wordlists for the Awbono-Bayono group (North Digul River family). Global Lexicostatistical Database, starlingdb.org.
sources.note: No statement. Re-transcribes Menanti's Awbono survey list from Wilbrink 2004: 108 into IPA/GLD; 10 of 64 Awbono entries carry a primary-stress mark ˈ, in varying positions: kˈoβo-kɑ 'ear', tˈɛkuru 'leg' (initial) vs ɑmˈɑ 'breast', ɛbˈi 'tooth', worˈai(-ɣɑ) 'stomach', dɛ-βˈu 'arm', babˈɪ 'head', bɑnˈɛ 'liver', yɑrˈi 'louse', bon-sˈɑmyɑ 'mouth' (final). Transcription note (p. 2) says Wilbrink's lists are 'standard IPA values throughout' and warns of inaccuracies.
sources.venue: Annotated Swadesh wordlists for the Awbono-Bayono group (North Digul River family)

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. 2018. GLD database description page for the Awbono-Bayono group (data sources and transcription notes).
sources.note: Nothing on stress; states 'Awbono and Bayono are attested solely through survey vocabularies, plus a handful of words in Hischier (2006)'.

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald. 2010. The status of the least documented language families in the world. Language Documentation & Conservation 4: 177-212, sect. 2.4.4 Bayono-Awbono (pp. 186-187).
sources.note: Nothing. 'The only data are the unpublished wordlists, including some sentences, of Mark Donohue and Phyllis Hischier (Hischier 2006), all of which were collected monolingually under challenging circumstances' (p. 187).

sources.citation: Wiktionary, Appendix: Bayono-Awbono word lists (reproducing Wilbrink 2004 lists for Awbono, Bayono, Kovojab, Densar).
sources.note: No statement; Awbono forms carry apostrophes before some syllables (bɑ'bʔ, e'bi, dɛ'βu, ɑ'mɑ, 'tɛkuru, kæ̃'dubi, bɑ'ri, gə'ni, ku'ru, jɑ'ri) which Usher 2018 reads as IPA stress marks; no notation key given.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Awbono language', 'Bayono–Awbono languages', 'Densar language'; Glottolog 5.x languoid page awbo1238.
sources.note: Nothing; 'All that is known of Awbono is a few hundred words recorded in first-contact situations' (Wilbrink 2004, Hischier 2006). Glottolog lists no descriptive refs beyond Wilbrink 2004 appendices and Hammarström 2010.

sources.citation: Whitehouse, Paul. n.d. Transcriptions of Menanti's Awbono and Bayono materials (cited by Usher 2018 as more accurate than Wilbrink's).

sources.note: Independent transcription of the same survey list; would confirm whether the apostrophes in Wilbrink are stress marks.

sources.citation: Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa. 2012 fieldwork behind Mukhamdanah & Inayatusshalihah 2021: 400-item Awban survey list (200 Swadesh + 200 cultural), Kampung Awban, Distrik Seredela, Kab. Yahukimo / Distrik Kolf Braza, Kab. Asmat.

sources.note: Collected by a trained phonetician-linguist; the only Awbono data by a linguist, likely with stress/tone marking.
